summary: An indology and philosophy scholar, Anantasharma B. G. earned degrees from National Sanskrit University, University of Madras, S-VYASA, and a PhD from Central Sanskrit University. Career posts include headships at Veda Vijnana Shodha Samsthana, Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, and Chanakya University.

Working in indology, philosophy, and history/archaeology, Ananya Vajpeyi studied at the University of Delhi, JNU, Oxford, Exeter College, and earned her PhD from the University of Chicago. She held posts at Columbia University and the Centre for the Study of Developing Societies.

Anastasiya Lozhkina specializes in indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Moscow State University, and became a junior research fellow at the Russian Academy of Sciences in 2018.

Anatol Waag was an Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics scholar who studied under Johannes Hertel and earned his PhD at the University of Leipzig. He held posts at Leipzig, the University of Zagreb, and the Institut für Deutsche Volkskunde.
Anatoli Guenko studied under Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay and Boris Turayev around 1914–1918.
Anders Hilding Andersson was an Indologist who completed his M.A. and Ph.D. at Lund University. In 1879, he became Docent of Greek Literature at Lund University.

Andrea Acri is a scholar of indology and religious studies who earned his PhD at Leiden University under Arlo Griffiths and Willem van der Molen. He has held positions at Leiden, EPHE, and the École française d'Extrême-Orient.

Andrea R. Jain is a scholar of religious studies and indology who earned degrees from Southern Methodist University and Rice University (PhD). She held faculty posts at IUPUI and Indiana University Bloomington, becoming full professor in 2021.

Andrea Schlosser is an indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her degrees from the Free University of Berlin. She has held research posts at the University of Munich and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Andreas Bock-Raming works in indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Paul Hacker and is attested as a researcher at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and tibetology, Andreas Doctor completed his PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura. He studied under several traditional Rinpoches and held a post at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Andreas Gottlieb Hoffmann was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He earned his doctorate at the University of Halle-Wittenberg under Wilhelm Gesenius, served as PD there, and became Professor of Theology at the University of Jena in 1826.
Andreas N. Kephallenos was a scholar of indology and linguistics. He completed his studies at the University of Florence and earned a Ph.D. from the University of Munich.
Andreas Spengel was a linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Munich and Frederick William University Berlin. He taught Albert Grünwedel.

Andree Dominique Messent specializes in Buddhist studies. Messent completed a PhD at the University of Bristol under the doctoral supervision of Paul Williams and also studied under Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.

Andrei Vostrikov was a tibetology, indology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy and Boris Vladimirtsov. He worked at the Asiatic Museum, Institute of Buddhist Culture, and Leningrad Institute of Living Oriental Languages.

Andrej Evgen’evič Snesarev worked in Central Asian studies, history/archaeology, and indology after studying at Moscow State University and the General Staff Academy. He served as Head of the General Staff Academy and Rector of the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies.
Andrew B. Irvine is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his PhD from Boston University. He was attested as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Maryville College in 2009.
Andrew Garrett is a scholar of linguistics and indology who earned his PhD from Harvard University in 1990. He became a professor at the University of California, Berkeley in 1995.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, indology, and linguistics, Andrew Glass earned his MA and PhD from the University of Washington, the latter supervised by Richard G. Salomon. He also studied at Bukkyo University.
